translations.text: And I stood on the mountain forty days and forty nights, and the Lord heard me at that time and did not wish to destroy you.
And the Lord said to me: "Go, set out before this people, and let them go in and take possession of the land which I swore to their fathers to give them."
And now you, too, are only men; or has wisdom come to an end with you?
For my heart, too, is like yours; I am not more foolish than you. For a righteous and blameless man has become a byword.
For at an appointed time he was made ready to fall at the hands of others, and his houses to be plundered by the lawless.
But let no one who is wicked trust that he will be innocent, nor anyone who provokes the Lord, as though there would be no judgment for him.
But ask the four-footed beasts, and see whether they will tell you anything. Speak to the earth, and see whether it will say anything to you, or whether the fish of the sea will tell it to you.
Who among all these does not know that the hand of the Lord made this?
Is not the soul of all living things in his hand, and the breath of every man?
For the mind judges words, and the palate tastes food. Is not wisdom found through long time, or knowledge through length of days?
From him come wisdom and power; counsel and understanding are his. If he tears down, who will build up?
Or if he shuts men in, who else will open? If he holds back the water, he dries up the earth; if he lets it loose, he destroys the earth all at once and overturns it.
From him come strength and power; knowledge and understanding are his.
He sends counselors into captivity and confounds the judges of the earth. He seats kings on thrones and girds them with the belt of might.
He sends priests away into captivity and overthrows the mighty of the earth. He alters the lips of the faithful, and he knows the understanding of the elders.
He pours contempt on rulers and heals the lowly. He brings the depths of darkness out into light from the shadows of death.
He leads the nations astray and lets them go; he brings down the sons of the tribes and leads them.
He alters the hearts of the rulers of the earth and makes them stray on a road they did not know.
They walk in darkness and not in light, and they wander like drunkards.
Behold, my eye has seen all this, and my ear has heard it. And I know as much as you know, and I have no less understanding than you.
Not only that, but I would speak to the Lord, and I will argue my case before him, if he wishes.
But you are all false physicians and evil comforters. If only you would keep silent, and it would be counted to you as wisdom.
Hear the reproofs of my mouth, and pay attention to the judgment of my lips.
What is this? Do you not speak before the Lord, and plot deceit in his presence?
Or will you hold yourselves back and make yourselves judges? Would it be good if he searched you out as well?
If you abandon it, it will become desolate; grass will spring up in it and it will become completely desolate, and its stone walls will be torn down.
Afterwards I repented and looked to choose instruction: "I sleep a little, and I fold my hands on my breast a little."
If you do this, your poverty will come upon you like a forerunner, and your want like a good runner.
The leech had three daughters, dearly loved, and all three of them could not satisfy her, and the fourth was not content to say, "Enough."
Hell, and the love of women, and Tartarus, and the earth that is never filled with water. Water and fire have not said, "Enough."
The eyes that mock a father and despise a mother's old age: let the ravens of the valley pluck them out, and let the young of the eagle devour them.
There are three things that are impossible for me, and the fourth I could not understand:
the track of an eagle in flight, the way of a serpent on a rock, the paths of a ship's passage, [?] [one that is appointed?], and the ways of a man in his youth.
Such is the way of an adulterous [?] woman: when she has done it, she washes herself and then says, "I have done nothing wrong."
By three things the earth is shaken, and the fourth I cannot bear: if a slave becomes king, and if a fool is filled with bread;
and if a maidservant drives out her mistress, and if a hateful wife gets a good husband.
There are four things that are the smallest on the earth, and they are wiser than the wise: the ants, which have no strength, yet prepare their food in summer;
and the rock badgers, a feeble kind, which make their nests in the rocks; the locust has no king, yet at a single command it marches in good order;
the lizard [?] holds fast to the wall with its hands, and though it is easy to catch, it lives in royal palaces.
There are three things that walk well, and a fourth that goes along well: the lion's cub, strongest of beasts, which does not turn back and is not terrified by any wild animal;
the cock, which walks at ease among the hens; the he-goat, leader of the flocks; and the king who makes proclamation to the nations.
If you give yourself over to pleasure and put out your hand in a quarrel against your own face [?], you will be disgraced. Churn milk and it becomes butter.
If you squeeze the nose [?], blood comes out. If you draw out empty words, judgments and quarrels come out.
The words were spoken by God: the command of a king, which his mother taught him. What, my son, is keeping God's word before everything else?
I tell you, my son, what is it, son of my womb? What is it, son of our prayers?
Do not give your wealth to women, or your mind and your life to deficient counsel. Do everything with counsel; drink wine with counsel.
The mighty are quick to anger when they drink wine. So let them not drink, or they will forget wisdom and be unable to judge the weak rightly.
Strong drink is given to those in grief, and wine to drink to those in distress, so that they may forget their poverty and no longer remember their sufferings.
Open your mouth with the word of God, and judge everyone soundly.
Open your mouth and judge the poor and the weak with righteousness.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
You shall go on your breast and belly, and you shall eat earth all the days of your life.
I will put enmity between you and the woman, between you and her offspring. He shall watch for your head, and you shall watch for his heel.
And to the woman he said: I will greatly multiply your sorrows and your sighs, and your turning shall be toward your husband,
and he shall rule over you. And to Adam he said: Because you listened to the voice of your wife, and because you ate from the tree
from which I commanded you not to eat, cursed be the earth in your works; in sorrow you shall eat all the days of your life.
It shall bring forth thorns and thistles for you, and you shall eat the grass of the field.
By the sweat of your face you shall eat your bread, until you return to the earth there, for you are earth and to earth you shall return.
And Adam called the name of his wife [?] Life, for she is the mother of all the living.
And God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife, and clothed them.
And God said: Behold, Adam has become like one of us, knowing good and evil.
Now then, he may put forth his hand and eat from the tree, and live forever.
And the Lord sent him out of the garden of delight, and set there the cherubim and the flaming, turning sword to guard the way of the tree of life.
And he set there the flaming cherubim and the turning sword to guard from the tree of life.
And it came to pass after these words that God tested Abraham and said to him: Abraham, Abraham. And Abraham said: Here I am, Lord.
And he said to him: Take your beloved son Isaac and go to a certain high land, and there offer him as a sacrifice on a certain mountain, which I tell you.
Abraham rose at dawn and saddled his donkey, and took with him two servants and Isaac his son;
and he split wood for the sacrifice, rose, and went to the place which God had told him.
Abraham lifted up his eyes, and behold, he saw the place from afar. And Abraham said to his servants:
Sit here with the donkeys; I and this boy will go to a certain place, worship the Lord, and come back to you.
And Abraham took the wood for the sacrifice and laid it on Isaac his son. And he took the fire and the knife in his hand, and the two of them went on together.
Isaac said to his father: Father. And he said: What is it, my son? And he said: Here are the fire and the wood; where is the sheep for the sacrifice?
Abraham said to him: God will see to a sheep for himself for the sacrifice, my son. And the two of them went on to the place which God had told him.
And Abraham built an altar of the Lord there, laid out the wood, bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar on top of the wood.
And he put out his hand to take the knife and to slay his son. And the angel of God spoke to him from heaven and said: Abraham, Abraham.
And he said: Here I am, Lord. And he said: Do not lay your hand on the boy, and do him no harm at all.
Who is this who hides his counsel from me, who gathers up thoughts in his heart and thinks to conceal them from me?
Gird up your loins like a man; I will question you, and you shall answer me: Where were you when I was laying the foundations of the earth?
Tell me, if you have understanding. Who set its measurements, do you know? Or who stretched the measuring line over it?
Or on what are its rings fastened? Or who is it that laid the corner stone upon it?
When the stars were made, all my angels praised me with a loud voice. I shut up the sea with gates when it was being born, when it came forth from its mother's womb.
I put a cloud on it as a garment and wrapped it in mists.
I set boundaries for it and fixed bars and gates for it, and I said to it: This far you shall come and no farther, but your waves shall be broken within you.
Or was it in your time that I appointed the light of dawn, and did the morning star learn its proper place from you, so as to reach the edges of the earth and scatter the ungodly from it?
Or did you take soil from the ground and make clay into a living, speaking being, and set it on the earth?
And the hand of the Lord was upon me, and he brought me out by the Spirit of God and set me down in the middle of a plain; and it was full of human bones.
And he led me over them; and behold, there were very many on the face of the plain, and they were very dry.
And he said to me: Son of man, prophesy over these bones. And say to them: You dry bones, hear the word of the Lord!
Thus says the Lord to these bones: Behold, I will send the spirit of life into you.
And I will put sinews on you, and make flesh grow on you, and spread skin over you;
and I will put my spirit in you, and you shall live, and you shall know that I am the Lord. And I prophesied as the Lord commanded me.
And it came to pass that as soon as I prophesied, behold, there was a shaking, and the bones were brought together, from both sides, each to its own joint. And I saw:
behold, sinews grew on them, and skin was spreading over them, but there was not yet any spirit in them.
And the Lord said to me: Prophesy, son of man, and say to the spirit: Thus says the Lord: Come from the four winds and breathe into these dead, and let them live!
And I prophesied as the Lord commanded me. The spirit entered into them, and they stood up on their feet, a very great multitude.
The Lord spoke to me and said: Son of man, these bones are the house of Israel, and they have all said:
'Our bones have dried up, and all our hope has perished, for we have died.' Therefore prophesy, son of man, and say to them:
Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will open your graves and bring you out of your graves, and I will bring you into the land of Israel.
And you shall know that I am the Lord, when I open your graves and bring my people out of their graves,
and I will put my spirit in you and bring you into your own land, and you shall know that I am the Lord, says the Lord of hosts.
And it came to pass after those words:
Who is this who hides his counsel from me, who gathers up thoughts in his heart and thinks to conceal them from me?
Gird up your loins like a man; I will question you, and you shall answer me: Where were you when I was laying the foundations of the earth?
Tell me, if you have understanding. Who set its measurements, do you know? Or who stretched the measuring line over it?
Or on what are its rings fastened? Or who is it that laid the corner stone upon it?
When the stars were made, all my angels praised me with a loud voice. I shut up the sea with gates when it was being born, when it came forth from its mother's womb.
I put a cloud on it as a garment and wrapped it in mists.
I set boundaries for it and fixed bars and gates for it, and I said to it: This far you shall come and no farther, but your waves shall be broken within you.
Or was it in your time that I appointed the light of dawn, and did the morning star learn its proper place from you, so as to reach the edges of the earth and scatter the ungodly from it?
Or did you take soil from the ground and make clay into a living, speaking being, and set it on the earth?
For they shall see and know and understand and believe together that the hand of the Lord made all this, and the Holy One of Israel revealed it.
It is not that I have now called you, Jacob, nor have I wearied you, Israel;
you did not bring me anything of your sacrifices, nor did you glorify me with your offerings; I did not make you serve me with offerings, nor did I weary you over incense;
nor did you buy me fragrant incense with silver, nor did I desire the fat of your sacrifices; instead, your sins and your falsehoods stood before you.
I am the one who wipes out your iniquities for my own sake, and I will no longer remember your sins.
But you, remember, and let us go to judgment together. State your iniquity first, so that you may be justified.
Your fathers sinned first, and your rulers acted lawlessly against me.
And your rulers defiled my sanctuary; I handed Jacob over to destruction and Israel to reproach.
But you, hear, Jacob my servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen.
Thus says the Lord God, who made you and who formed you from your mother's womb:
I have helped you.
Let the heavens rejoice and let the earth be glad, for God has had mercy on Israel;
blow the trumpet, foundations of the earth; and cry out with joy, mountains and hills and all their trees, for the Lord has redeemed Jacob, and Israel shall glorify him.
Thus says the Lord, your Redeemer, who formed you from the womb: I am the Lord, who made all things, and I alone stretched out the heavens and made the earth firm.
Who else, then, will bring it to nothing? I am the one who brings to nothing the signs of the ventriloquists and the divinations of the heart;
I have turned the wise backward and made their counsels foolish; and I will confirm the word of my servant, and the counsel of his messengers shall prove true;
for it is he who says to Jerusalem, 'Be inhabited,' and 'Let the cities of Judah be built, and let its desolate places be raised up';
who says to the abyss, 'Be laid waste!' and 'I will dry up your rivers'; who says to Cyrus, 'Be wise!'
'and all your will shall be done'; who says to Jerusalem, 'Be rebuilt!' and 'I will lay the foundation of my holy temple.'
Thus says the Lord our God to my anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have held,
to make the nations submit to him; and I will shatter the strength of kings; I will open gates before him, and his cities shall not be shut.
I went before him and leveled the mountains, and I broke in pieces the gates of bronze and shattered the bolts of iron.
And I will give you the treasures of darkness, hidden ones, and I will open to you unseen ones, so that you may know that I am the Lord God,
who called you by your name, the name of Israel [?], for the sake of my servant Jacob and Israel my chosen one, and I received you.
For you did not know me; for I am the Lord your God, and there is no one besides me, and you did not know me,
